steps.say: Runs on the hardware you already have.

steps.caption: llama.cpp v1.0.0, 13 November
steps.say: Runs every model. And now, for the first time, a major version. So what does the one in front of the dot actually promise?

scenes.headline: What llama.cpp 1.0 promises, and what it does not
scenes.sub: Read from the diff between two tags
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wexley. I diffed the last zero release against one point oh. Here is where the promise starts and stops.

steps.say: For years, llama.cpp had no versions, only build numbers. This release was cut from nightly twelve thousand three hundred and fifty-nine.
Eleven more tags in three months. Under zero point x, any of them was allowed to break anything.

steps.term: Major version: bumped when the C API breaks
steps.say: One point oh changes the rule. A breaking change to the headers in include now bumps the major, and the library's soname follows it.

params.shift: Everything after byte 120 moves 8 bytes later
params.wrong: An old binary's fields land on the wrong ones

steps.say: Callers pass this struct by value, so its layout is compiled into every program. Here it is from byte eighty on.
One point oh deletes a deprecated float. But a pointer has to start on a multiple of eight, so the gap becomes padding and nothing moves.
The new field is what breaks it. A float at byte one hundred and twenty, and every field after it slides eight bytes.
A binary built against the old header would hand its callback to the wrong field, silently. That is what the soname bump catches.
Now the file. A GGUF starts with a magic word, a version, and two counts.

steps.term: GGUF: metadata, tensor records, then aligned data
steps.say: Then metadata, then one record per tensor with its type and an offset. The data is stored exactly as the kernels read it, so loading is a memory map.

states.say: I parsed one real file by range request: a hundred and forty-seven tensors.

states.term: Q4_K_M is a recipe that mixes types, not a type
states.say: Sorted by type, Q4_K_M turns out to be a mix. The embedding and half the down projections stay at six bits.

scenes.title: A version 3 file that will not load

left.title: The container
left.say: Here is a file from 2024 in the same repository. As a container, it is perfectly valid version three.

right.title: The type ids
right.say: But most of its tensors use a type that was removed, and the reader stops at the first one. One point oh promises nothing about GGUF.

scenes.title: Decode tok/s, RTX 3090, 1B Q4_K_M
scenes.note: mean of five runs, standard deviation about 3%
scenes.say: I built both releases on a three-oh-ninety and ran the same files. Decode speed did not move: every gap is inside the noise.

scenes.title: Decode tok/s, four quants, v1.0.0
scenes.say: The quant matters more than the release. Smaller files decode faster, until the codebook formats: the smallest file here is slower than Q4_0.

scenes.text: 1.0 binds the C headers and the soname. GGUF stays version 3, and old type ids can still disappear.
scenes.mark: old type ids can still disappear
scenes.say: One point oh binds the C headers and the soname. Your GGUF files are on their own: keep the source checkpoint.

recap: A break to include/ bumps the major
The new field moved the struct, not the deletion
GGUF is still version 3, no promise
scenes.say: The headers are promised, the struct moved for a new field, and GGUF has no promise. Thanks for watching!
